t: Kerma grew from a fortified village into a city of about 25 hectares, the capital of a centralised Nubian kingdom that controlled the Nile from the First to the Fourth Cataract.
Rich in gold, cattle, ivory and ebony, it traded with Egypt and fought it, raiding deep into Egypt around 1575–1550 BCE in alliance with the Hyksos.
Thutmose I of Egypt destroyed Kerma around 1504 BCE, but rebellions went on for two centuries, and the later Kingdom of Kush honoured Kerma as part of its past.
dyk: Egyptian royal statues and monuments looted in Kerma’s raid on Egypt were carried back to Kerma, and the defeat is believed to have been erased later from Egypt’s official records; it is known from an inscription in the tomb of the governor Sobeknakht II at Nekheb.
ev: The pre-Kerma culture develops in Upper Nubia, with small kingdoms and settled farming
A new fortified village at Kerma begins the Early Kerma period
Egypt’s Middle Kingdom builds forts in Lower Nubia, while Kerma fortifies Sai as its border
The Classic Kerma period begins: the city grows to about 25 hectares and the Western Deffufa is built
Kerma, allied with the Hyksos, invades deep into Egypt
After the campaigns of Thutmose I, Egypt annexes Kerma
George Andrew Reisner excavates Kerma, taking it for an Egyptian outpost
Charles Bonnet’s Swiss team finds a cache of granite statues of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty pharaohs at Kerma

f.homeland: Upper Nubia, in present-day northern and central Sudan, centred on Kerma; at its height from the First to the Fourth Cataract; key sites Kerma with its Western Deffufa, Doukki Gel and Sai Island
f.period: Pre-Kerma c. 3500–2500 BCE; Early Kerma c. 2500–2000 BCE; Middle Kerma c. 2000–1750 BCE; Classic Kerma c. 1750–1500 BCE; conquered by Egypt c. 1504 BCE, with rebellions until c. 1300 BCE
f.known: the Western Deffufa, a monumental mudbrick temple; great royal tumuli with human sacrifices; cattle skulls buried with kings; an army of archers; trade in gold, ivory, ebony and incense; the raid into Egypt c. 1575–1550 BCE
f.sources: excavations at Kerma by George Andrew Reisner (1920s) and Charles Bonnet; surveys along the Nile and before the Merowe Dam; Egyptian inscriptions and records; ceramic sequences; skeletal and dental studies; ancient DNA (2022)
